name: Jethro/Reuel (Moses' father-in-law)
title: Priest of Midian and wise counselor
summary: Jethro, also called Reuel, was a priest in Midian and the father of Zipporah, who became Moses' wife. He welcomed Moses when he fled from Egypt and later gave him wise advice on delegating leadership, which became foundational for Israel's organization.

keyEvents.title: Moses flees to Midian
keyEvents.description: Moses fled from Egypt after killing an Egyptian and arrived in Midian, where he met Jethro's daughters at a well and was welcomed into his home.

keyEvents.title: Moses marries Zipporah
keyEvents.description: Jethro gave his daughter Zipporah to Moses as a wife, and Moses stayed with him and tended his flocks.

keyEvents.title: Jethro hears about Israel's deliverance
keyEvents.description: After the departure from Egypt, Jethro heard about all that God had done for Moses and Israel, and he took Zipporah and her sons to Moses in the wilderness.

keyEvents.title: Jethro Praises the Lord
keyEvents.description: When Jethro heard of God's mighty deeds, he confessed that the Lord is greater than all gods, and he brought burnt offerings and sacrifices to God.

keyEvents.title: Advice on Delegating Leadership
keyEvents.description: Jethro observed that Moses judged the people alone from morning until evening, and gave him wise counsel to appoint capable men as leaders over thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens to relieve his burden.

keyEvents.title: Jethro Returns Home
keyEvents.description: After giving his advice, Jethro took leave of Moses and returned to his own land.
